_comment: Golden SynthID-Text fixture inventory for markproof M3 (Art. 50 text marking). Generated by generate.py -- do not hand-edit.
_provenance: All texts are Tippel's own production: sampled token sequences built by generate.py, plus one hand-written English paragraph. No third-party text and no model output from any provider is present in this directory.

tokenizer.note: Tokenizer files only (vocab.json, merges.txt, tokenizer.json); no model weights are downloaded. Detection needs token ids, not a language model.

watermark_config_note: Identical in every fixture file. g-values are only comparable within one config: changing ngram_len, keys, sampling_table_size or sampling_table_seed invalidates every measured_mean_g below. The keys are the public example keys from the transformers docs and are TEST KEYS -- never mark production output with them.

statistic.definition: mean over all n-grams and all 9 key depths of compute_g_values(token_ids); no language model involved

thresholds.decision_rule: token_count < 100 -> skipped; mean_g <= 0.56 -> not_watermarked; mean_g >= 0.7 -> watermarked; otherwise -> uncertain
thresholds.rationale: Reproduce every number below with `python generate.py --sweep` (16 seeds per cell). min_tokens: sigma(100 n-grams) = 0.0167, so 0.56 sits 3.6 sigma above 0.5 for clean text at the floor; at 40 tokens the clean and the weakly-marked populations nearly touch (0.540 vs 0.565) and weakly marked text reaches 0.698, which any 0.70 threshold would call watermarked. lower: at >= 100 tokens the unwatermarked maximum was 0.519. upper: at the same lengths the watermarked minimum was 0.764, so 0.70 keeps ~0.06 of headroom while leaving the uncertain band wide enough that partly marked text (measured 0.586-0.657) lands inside it instead of on a verdict.

files.how_generated: 120 tokens; at every position from index 4 on, 16 candidates are drawn and the one whose n-gram carries the most g-bits wins (random.Random(seed=1101)). This reproduces SynthID tournament sampling with a uniform proposal distribution.
files.why_it_matters: Shortest fully marked text still above MIN_TOKENS. Proves the check fires at the floor and does not need a wall of text to reach a verdict.

files.how_generated: 240 tokens; at every position from index 4 on, 16 candidates are drawn and the one whose n-gram carries the most g-bits wins (random.Random(seed=1102)). This reproduces SynthID tournament sampling with a uniform proposal distribution.
files.why_it_matters: The ordinary marked case: a typical chatbot answer length, unambiguous signal.

files.how_generated: 480 tokens; at every position from index 4 on, 16 candidates are drawn and the one whose n-gram carries the most g-bits wins (random.Random(seed=1103)). This reproduces SynthID tournament sampling with a uniform proposal distribution.
files.why_it_matters: Long marked text. mean-g must stay ~0.78 and not drift with length -- a check that accumulates instead of averaging would show length dependence here.

files.how_generated: 120 tokens drawn uniformly at random (random.Random(seed=2101)) from the round-trip-safe GPT-2 word pool. No tournament, so every g-bit is a fair coin.
files.why_it_matters: Clean text at the length floor, where the statistic is noisiest. The false-positive case that decides whether MIN_TOKENS is set honestly.

files.how_generated: 240 tokens drawn uniformly at random (random.Random(seed=2102)) from the round-trip-safe GPT-2 word pool. No tournament, so every g-bit is a fair coin.
files.why_it_matters: The ordinary clean case. Must never be reported as marked.

files.how_generated: 480 tokens drawn uniformly at random (random.Random(seed=2103)) from the round-trip-safe GPT-2 word pool. No tournament, so every g-bit is a fair coin.
files.why_it_matters: Long clean text; mean-g converges tightly on 0.50.

files.how_generated: Hand-written English paragraph (Tippel's own text), tokenised with gpt2@607a30d. No watermarking of any kind.
files.why_it_matters: Real, human-written English rather than sampled tokens. The others prove the statistic behaves; this one proves it behaves on text a person would actually send.

files.how_generated: 160 tokens; the 16-candidate tournament runs at a randomly chosen 40% of positions and the remaining positions are drawn uniformly (random.Random(seed=3101)). Models text that is only partly machine generated, which is what lands the mean-g between the thresholds.
files.why_it_matters: Partly marked text, e.g. a marked draft a human rewrote. THE case that must come back uncertain: any verdict here is a guess dressed as evidence.

files.how_generated: 240 tokens; the 16-candidate tournament runs at a randomly chosen 42% of positions and the remaining positions are drawn uniformly (random.Random(seed=3102)). Models text that is only partly machine generated, which is what lands the mean-g between the thresholds.
files.why_it_matters: Same mechanism at ordinary length. Sits near the middle of the uncertain band, so it stays uncertain even if either threshold moves by 0.03.

files.how_generated: 400 tokens; the 16-candidate tournament runs at a randomly chosen 42% of positions and the remaining positions are drawn uniformly (random.Random(seed=3103)). Models text that is only partly machine generated, which is what lands the mean-g between the thresholds.
files.why_it_matters: Long partly-marked text. Length removes the excuse that the ambiguity is small-sample noise: the signal really is intermediate, and more tokens will not resolve it.

files.how_generated: 3 tokens drawn uniformly at random (random.Random(seed=4101)) from the round-trip-safe GPT-2 word pool. No tournament, so every g-bit is a fair coin.
files.why_it_matters: Fewer tokens than ngram_len, so compute_g_values() raises RuntimeError. The check must skip on token count BEFORE calling into transformers, not catch an exception.

files.how_generated: 5 tokens drawn uniformly at random (random.Random(seed=4102)) from the round-trip-safe GPT-2 word pool. No tournament, so every g-bit is a fair coin.
files.why_it_matters: Exactly ngram_len: one single n-gram. A number is produced (~0.33) and it is pure noise. Computable is not the same as meaningful.

files.how_generated: 24 tokens drawn uniformly at random (random.Random(seed=4103)) from the round-trip-safe GPT-2 word pool. No tournament, so every g-bit is a fair coin.
files.why_it_matters: A one-sentence reply. Plausible endpoint output, still far below the floor.

files.how_generated: 64 tokens; at every position from index 4 on, 16 candidates are drawn and the one whose n-gram carries the most g-bits wins (random.Random(seed=4104)). This reproduces SynthID tournament sampling with a uniform proposal distribution.
files.why_it_matters: The sharp one: genuinely watermarked, mean-g well above the upper threshold, but under MIN_TOKENS. It must STILL be skipped. Length gating has to run before the statistic, or the tool reports a verdict it cannot defend -- and the same gate that protects against false positives has to cost us this true positive.
